name: Alchemer
tagline: Surveys, workflows, feedback programs, and enterprise integrations

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 3 active or closed surveys and 100 responses per survey; standard reports plus CSV and Excel export

tiers.name: Collaborator
tiers.limits: Unlimited surveys and questions; 75,000 responses/year per account
tiers.notes: Annual price is $315/user/year. Monthly response limits also apply.

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: Unlimited surveys and questions; 100,000 responses/year per account; maximum 3 users on this self-serve tier
tiers.notes: Annual price is $1,075/user/year. Monthly response limits also apply.

tiers.name: Full Access
tiers.limits: Unlimited surveys and questions; 125,000 responses/year per account; maximum 3 users on this self-serve tier
tiers.notes: Annual price is $1,895/user/year. Monthly response limits also apply.

tiers.name: Business Platform
tiers.limits: For more than 3 users, API access, advanced administration and organization-wide programs; limits are custom

pricing.freeTierCaps: 3 active or closed surveys; 100 responses per survey; standard reports; CSV and Excel export
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual prepaid; 7-day trial is separate from the permanent free plan
pricing.hiddenCosts: Response allowances are account-wide and follow the highest license on the account rather than stacking per seat; more than 3 users and API access require a custom Business Platform plan.

verdictSummary: The visible enterprise surveys loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Alchemer earns its keep through delivery, integrations, compliance, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a enterprise surveys tool with a schema-based form editor, public share link, validation, response table, CSV export, and webhook.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: SMTP or transactional email key in .env
whatYouLose: resilient polling of malformed and rate-limited feeds
spam and abuse defense at scale
whyPeopleStillPay: Alchemer: Customers pay for dependable collection, spam control, notifications, integrations, and confidence that responses will not disappear.
ongoingBurden: Own storage, webhooks, email delivery, spam, file uploads, privacy requests, schema changes, and uptime.

rejectedAlternatives.name: HeyForm

rejectedAlternatives.name: LimeSurvey
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A deep survey engine, but not Alchemer’s workflow and feedback-program layer

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Alchemer is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Alchemer, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a enterprise surveys tool with a schema-based form editor, public share link, validation, response table, CSV export, and webhook.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: large integration and template catalog; compliance controls and guaranteed delivery; resilient polling of malformed and rate-limited feeds.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
